evidence_quotes.agenda: "I do wanna just make sure that I answer the most important questions that you have. So what would some of those... top of mind questions be." — asked before probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: First-time mover raises multiple real concerns (timeframe feasibility, packing assistance, whether she needs to be present); rep digs into each with genuine follow-up rather than a scripted pivot (e.g., clarifying exactly what "being present" means for her situation).
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: "you're only paying for the time you use... if they only use three or four hours the next day, that's all you end up paying for" (beats-it-pay-less) + a window statement tied to the two-day packing/load plan; no commit-to-rate line, no self-prep tip, no "does that feel fair" + silence.

top_strength: Exceptional discovery and patience with a nervous first-time mover on a complex two-day pack-and-store job — walks through the treadmill, storage-unit specifics, and presence-during-move policy with real care, and flexibly reworks the schedule around her work conflicts.
coaching_note: This is the strongest call in the batch and still lands just under the pass bar — Communication (Sheet 4) never got its own distinct mention, and none of the five closing lines ("does that feel fair?" + silence, self-prep tip, commit-to-rate) were used before booking; add those and this is an 85+ call.
